narrative.overview:
Clean, honest, utilitarian. The SMA-BE pricing system treats clarity as its entire personality — like a well-designed utility bill where every number is immediately findable and every condition is spelled out. The interface steps back so the pricing speaks.

The visual language is deliberately restrained: white cards on a warm grey canvas, a single green for all actionable elements, and purple reserved exclusively for promotional ribbons. Density is comfortable but not spacious — pricing comparisons need proximity to work.
keyCharacteristics: Subgrid-aligned cards ensure row-level horizontal consistency across products
Purple is promotional only — never structural, never decorative
Green is action only — CTA buttons and checkmarks, nothing else
Content-driven height — cards grow to fit, never pad to match

rules.name: The Two-Hue Rule
rules.body: Green and purple are the only chromatic colors in the system. Green means action; purple means promotion. If a new element needs color, it uses one of these two or it stays neutral.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only cards have shadows. Everything inside a card is flat. Depth is conveyed through background color, never through nested shadows.

rules.name: The Weight Rule
rules.body: Bold (700) means important or interactive. Regular (400) means informational. Light (300) means secondary context. No medium weights, no italic.

dos: Do use subgrid to keep card rows aligned — the entire comparison mechanic depends on horizontal consistency.
Do let cards grow to their content. A card with two features and one ribbon item is shorter; the subgrid handles it.
Do keep the ribbon visually attached to the card top — flush edges, no internal margin above.
Do use overflow: clip on cards to crop ribbon backgrounds cleanly at rounded corners.
donts: Don't use purple outside of promotional ribbons and conditional price boxes.
Don't add shadows to anything inside a card — only the card itself casts a shadow.
Don't use medium font weights (500/600) — the system uses only 300, 400, and 700.
Don't add icons to buttons — the CTA is text-only by design.
Don't force equal card heights by padding — let subgrid handle alignment naturally.
